title: How can we make the web a better place?
reason: 本集从近期的风险决策主题轮换到软件与数字生活，讨论 Web Science 如何同时研究技术、用户行为和社会影响，并以接触追踪应用说明产品宣称、技术机制和实际效果之间需要验证。内容贴近平台工程、系统设计与技术评估，适合反复调用日常工作中常见的说明、判断和验证表达。

targetExpressions.meaning: begin again from the start after losing progress or making a mistake
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when previous work cannot be continued: The failed migration forced us to start all over again.

targetExpressions.expression: with a click of a button
targetExpressions.meaning: very quickly and easily by using a computer or digital device
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to describe easy digital access: Users can generate the report with a click of a button.

targetExpressions.expression: act as a force for good
targetExpressions.meaning: have a positive influence on people or society
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to describe beneficial impact: Open standards can act as a force for good across the industry.

targetExpressions.meaning: include many different things between two stated examples
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to show variety: Platform risks range from service outages to data leaks.

targetExpressions.meaning: more complicated or difficult than it first appears
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to qualify a simple-looking claim: Replacing a legacy service is not that straightforward.

targetExpressions.expression: do what it says on the tin
targetExpressions.meaning: work exactly as its description or name promises
targetExpressions.usage: Use this informal expression when judging whether something performs as claimed: The tool is simple, but it does what it says on the tin.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Neil's reaction after his computer froze: He lost everything and had to ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil says the frozen computer erased his work, so he had to begin again from the start.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the description of modern technology: Computers and the internet can bring us the world ______.
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: with a click of a button
answers: with a click of a button
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript uses this phrase to emphasise how quickly and easily the internet provides access to information.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which statement best reflects the episode's description of the internet as a possible “force for good”?
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: act as a force for good

options.text: It can support progress, although it can also spread hate and misinformation.
It always benefits society and has no harmful effects.
It is useful only for academic researchers.
It should replace all face-to-face communication.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme contrasts the web's potential for good and progress with its ability to spread hate and misinformation.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the summary: Web Science combines subjects that ______ psychology and robotics to economics and sociology.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript says the interdisciplinary field draws on subjects ranging from psychology and robotics to economics and sociology.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Why does Carly Kind suggest that contact-tracing technology is “not that straightforward”?

options.text: It is still uncertain whether Bluetooth detects contact adequately and provides the needed public-health information.
Nobody knows how to install an app on a phone.
The app was designed only to share photographs.
The public-health goal had already been abandoned.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Carly questions both the adequacy of Bluetooth and whether the apps work in the intended way, so the apparently simple solution has unresolved problems.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: In the episode, what does it mean for a mechanism to “do what it says on the tin”?
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: do what it says on the tin

options.text: It performs exactly as intended or promised.
It is stored inside a metal container.
It is popular even though it does not work.
It requires no testing or evidence.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript defines the idiom as working exactly as something is intended to work.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: According to the programme, what is needed before deciding that an app does what it says on the tin?
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: do what it says on the tin

options.text: Trials that test how effective and suitable it is over time
A more attractive icon and a shorter name
A promise from the first person who downloads it
Removal of all public-health requirements

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme explains that trials are tests carried out over time to discover whether something is effective or suitable.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which sentence uses “not that straightforward” naturally in a software project?

options.text: The feature looks small, but migrating the old data is not that straightforward.
The feature not straightforward that the data.
We straightforward the migration yesterday.
The data is not that straightforwardly a feature.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The natural pattern is a situation or task + is not that straightforward, meaning it is more complicated than it appears.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80–120 words using this structure: (1) topic—what Web Science studies; (2) two key ideas—how people and technology form an ecosystem, and why the contact-tracing app needs evidence; (3) conclusion—how the web might help society. Phrase bank: “act as a force for good”, “not that straightforward”, “do what it says on the tin”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate sentences are enough.
referencePoints: Web Science studies both internet technology and how people interact online.
The web is co-created by society because people add content and interact through platforms and social networks.
Web Science is interdisciplinary, combining technology with fields such as psychology, robotics, economics and sociology.
Humans and technology form an ecosystem with complex relationships and mutual influences.
A contact-tracing app aims to support public health, but Bluetooth may not detect contact adequately or provide the information needed.
Trials are needed to determine whether an app is effective, suitable and works as intended.
